article.Citation/Title: Thurgur, H., Sessa, B., Higbed, L., O'Brien, S., Durant, C., Wilson, S., Szigeti, B., Morgan, C. J. A., & Nutt, D. J. (2025). MDMA-assisted psychotherapy for AUD: Bayesian analysis of WHO drinking risk level and exploratory analysis of drinking behavior and psychosocial functioning at 3 months follow-up. Alcohol and Alcoholism, 60, agaf031.
article.Outcome: 0.63 posterior probability of a ≥2-level WHO drinking-risk reduction at 3 months (flat prior)
article.InterventionDescription: MDMA-assisted psychotherapy: initial 125mg oral MDMA plus 62.5mg booster across 2 of 10 sessions in an 8-week course; open-label, UK trial center, overnight stay post-dosing.

article.Citation/Title: This is a secondary/Bayesian re-analysis of data from the parent open-label feasibility trial Sessa B, Higbed L, O'Brien S, et al. 'First study of safety and tolerability of 3,4-methylenedioxymethamphetamine-assisted psychotherapy in patients with alcohol use disorder.' J Psychopharmacol (Oxf). 2021;35:375-83. https://doi.org/10.1177/0269881121991792. Same 14 participants, same trial (NCT04158778); this paper reanalyzes drinking-risk and secondary PROM data at the 3-month timepoint. Eligible under the secondary-analysis boundary case in the prompt.
article.Outcome: Abstract/Results/Table 1: primary analysis of this paper is the Bayesian posterior probability of a 2-level reduction in WHO drinking risk level at 3 months, with 9/14 participants meeting the success threshold. Chose the flat-prior mean posterior (0.63) over the skeptical-prior estimate (0.55) as the primary value since Table 1 lists it first and it is the uninformative/reference prior; the skeptical-prior result is the sensitivity analysis. Note the Abstract's phrasing ('55%-63%...flat or skeptical prior respectively') orders the two priors oppositely to the Results/Table 1 text (flat=63%, skeptical=55%) -- the numeric values themselves are consistent across Abstract, Results text, and Table 1, only the prose ordering in the Abstract is inconsistent, so this is flagged as a wording issue, not a numeric discrepancy per Non-negotiable #2.
article.SD: Table 1 / Results paragraph: flat-prior 95% credible interval 0.40-0.85, paired with the flat-prior mean posterior (0.63) chosen for Outcome.
article.SampleSize_NFinal: Table 1: WHO drinking-risk Bayesian analysis sample size = 14 (all enrolled participants; Demographics section confirms 14 enrolled, 8 male/6 female).
article.Pos Result Y/N: Judged on the study's own pre/post direction (single-arm, no comparator). 9/14 (64%) participants achieved the 2-level WHO risk reduction success threshold, and the Bayesian posterior probability of success was 55-63%, which the Discussion frames as comparable to a 68% two-level reduction rate reported for established AUD treatments (COMBINE/Project MATCH secondary analysis). Multiple secondary PROMs also showed significant improvement (PACS P=.031, OCDS obsessive P=.006 and compulsive P=.021, PSQI sleep P=.041, self-compassion P<.001, IRI personal-distress P=.009). Coded 1 (positive) despite the preliminary binomial test against a 50% null being non-significant (P=.423), since that frequentist test is not the primary analysis and direction is not ambiguous or mixed.
article.Clincial Trial YN: Coded 1, consistent with EligibleYN=Y via the secondary-analysis boundary case: this article reanalyzes data from a prospectively conducted open-label clinical trial (Sessa et al. 2021, same cohort/protocol), so criterion (a) of the eligibility screen is satisfied through that boundary case rather than through this paper itself being a new prospective trial.
article.Retention (%): Denominator is enrolled N since the study was not randomized (single-arm). Abstract/Demographics: 14 enrolled, and Table 1's primary WHO-risk Bayesian analysis includes all 14 (14/14 = 100%). Smaller per-instrument analysis Ns reported in Figures 2-3 (PACS/OCDS n=13, PSQI n=14, SCS n=13, IRI n=12, SF-36 n=11) reflect instrument-specific missing PROM data at 3 months, not overall study attrition from the enrolled cohort, so they were not used as the retention numerator.
article.BaseStatus: Coded '.': the article states participants had an AUD diagnosis and had 'recently undergone detoxification' but gives no explicit severity classification (e.g., DSM-5 criterion count or a Mild/Moderate/Severe descriptor) for this cohort within this text.
article.PercentFem: Demographics: 'The study enrolled 14 participants (8 males and 6 females...)'. 6/14 = 42.86%.
article.RaceEthnicity_BIPOCPercent: Demographics: 'All were white British.' BIPOC percent = 0.
article.Country_USvsNonUS: Trial sponsored by Imperial College London, approved by the South West-Central Bristol Research Ethics Committee (UK) and MHRA; corresponding author affiliation London, UK. Coded 'NonUS'; country is United Kingdom.
article.SocioeconomicStatusYN: No income, insurance status, or SES-related eligibility criteria described anywhere in the article.
article.RecruitmentRepresentYN: Coded 0: the Limitations section lists substantial exclusion criteria (antidepressant use, serious suicide risk, comorbid psychotic/personality disorders, cardiovascular/severe liver disease) and explicitly states the study 'lacked ethnic diversity' (all-white-British sample), indicating a highly screened, non-representative sample rather than a real-world clinical population.
article.MediatingYN: The Discussion states 'Future studies should determine whether craving mediates or predicts outcome response' — an explicit statement that no mediation analysis was run in this study, only proposed for future work. Craving (a candidate mediator) was measured as an outcome (PACS/OCDS), so the concept applies; coded 0, not 3.
article.ModeratingYN: No interaction term, subgroup-by-treatment test, or stratified effect-modification analysis is reported anywhere. Candidate moderators (age, sex) were measured as demographics, so the concept applies; coded 0, not 3.
article.HypothesisTestReportedYN: The primary WHO-drinking-risk-reduction classification was tested with a binomial test against a 50% expected success rate (k=.64, P=.423) and framed with Bayesian credible intervals excluding the flat-prior default of 50% only partially (both intervals span >50%, so this is not itself a significance claim, but the binomial P-value itself is the reported inferential test). Coded 1 because an inferential test was reported for the primary comparison, regardless of its non-significant result.
article.Power: No a priori or post hoc power calculation or discussion is present anywhere in the article; only sample size (n=14) and 'small population'/'small sample size' limitations are mentioned, which is distinct from a power discussion per the field rule.
article.SafetyReported: Judgment call, flagged per Non-negotiable #5 (understating harm is the cardinal AE error). This paper's own Methods/Results explicitly defer AE reporting to the parent publication: 'adverse events, all of which have been previously reported (Sessa et al. 2021)'. However, the Introduction also states, describing this same 14-participant trial, 'MDMA was well-tolerated and no unexpected adverse events were observed.' Because the article affirmatively states harms were assessed (even though full detail lives in the parent paper), coding SafetyReported='N' would incorrectly imply 'the authors never looked', which the prompt identifies as the worse error. Coded 'Y'.
article.AnyAEReported: 'No unexpected adverse events were observed' is standard trial-safety phrasing implying expected/anticipated AEs did occur but nothing outside the anticipated safety profile -- it is not equivalent to 'no AEs occurred'. Per the cardinal rule against understating harm, coded 'Y' rather than collapsing this into a zero-AE reading.
article.NumDistinctAEs: This article names no individual AE types, counts, or a table -- it only carries forward the single summary clause above from the parent trial. Coded 'Not numbered' rather than fabricating a count or a specific AE type.
article.WorstSeverity: No severity-relevant detail (intervention required, functional impairment, seriousness criteria) is present in this article's text for any AE. Defaulted to 'Mild' per the rubric's under-specified-AE default (Severity rubric, 'Under-specified AEs' section), since no signal of escalation is present. This default could not be attached to a distinct ae_events row because no AE type is nameable from this text without consulting the parent Sessa et al. 2021 article, which is out of scope for this extraction; ae_events is therefore empty despite AnyAEReported='Y'. This whole AE block is a genuinely non-obvious judgment call and would benefit from human review against the parent article.
article.HarmsAssessed: Set to 1 to agree with SafetyReported='Y' per the required HarmsAssessed/SafetyReported concordance rule.

MethodologyDescribedYN.note: sample_size_power is the only unmet criterion: sample size (n=14) is stated but no a priori or post hoc power calculation is discussed anywhere. comparator, randomization and blinding are each counted as met because their absence is explicitly described ('open-label' stated repeatedly; Limitations calls for 'larger and randomized placebo-controlled trials'; Discussion explicitly addresses the challenge of blinding MDMA), consistent with the rule that describing an element as absent satisfies the criterion. setting is minimally but genuinely described (Imperial College London sponsor, UK REC/MHRA approval, overnight stay at the treatment center after dosing sessions, per Future Directions). harms is met because the article states AEs were assessed and reported (in the parent publication), even though it does not re-tabulate them here. n_met=13 meets the >=13 threshold, so MethodologyDescribedYN=1.

config_proposal.metric: Bayesian posterior probability (single-arm binomial success rate)
config_proposal.measure: 9/14 (Bayesian posterior probability of treatment success: 0.63 flat prior, 0.55 skeptical prior)
config_proposal.note: The study's primary statistic is a Bayesian posterior probability of a binary treatment-success outcome (2-level WHO drinking-risk reduction) derived from a single-arm 9/14 success rate with flat and skeptical priors. A Bayesian posterior probability is not one of the seven supported conversion methods (d, g, eta_p, F, chi2, OR, RR), and there is no comparator arm from which to compute an OR/RR; no defensible conversion to Hedges' g exists.
config_proposal.tier2_basis: Single-arm, open-label secondary analysis; 9/14 (64%) participants achieved the pre-defined 2-level WHO drinking-risk reduction success threshold, with Bayesian posterior probability of success 55-63% depending on prior, and multiple secondary craving/sleep/self-compassion PROMs improved significantly at 3 months -- directionally positive though the preliminary frequentist binomial test against a 50% null was not significant (P=.423).
